tracks.title: The paper in 5 minutes
tracks.desc: The whole study as a simple story, in plain words only, with a one-page map and the 831 → 80 → 9 → 5 → 2 funnel.

tracks.title: Biology from zero
tracks.desc: Cells, DNA, genes, RNA, proteins, and long noncoding RNAs — everything you need before the paper makes sense.

tracks.title: Cancer from zero
tracks.desc: What cancer is, lung cancer, KRAS, cisplatin, cell lines vs normal cells, 3D models, mice, and patient datasets.

tracks.title: Lab tools from zero
tracks.desc: CRISPR, viruses, pooled screens, ASOs and every validation assay in the paper, plus RNA-seq and pathways.

tracks.title: Numbers & statistics from zero
tracks.desc: CPM/TPM/FPKM, fold change and log2, replicates, correlation, p-values, FDR, ROC/AUC and the paper's TPP pipeline.

tracks.title: How to read figures
tracks.desc: One mini-lesson per chart type in the paper, each practised on a real panel.

tracks.title: The paper, section by section
tracks.desc: The core: every paragraph (verbatim) with Plain English, why it matters, prerequisites and check questions, plus a guide to every figure panel.

tracks.title: Critical thinking
tracks.desc: Claims and evidence, controls, alternative explanations, limitations, the patent, strengthening experiments, strengths vs weaknesses.

lessons.title: The whole study as a simple story
lessons.goal: Follow the whole paper from question to answer in plain words: what the authors wanted to know, what they did, what they found, and what they did next.
lessons.notes: Plain words only. Every word that is a technical term in the glossary must either be avoided or explained in one plain sentence right where it is first used (list those in `defines`).

lessons.title: One-page map of the pipeline
lessons.goal: See the whole pipeline as one picture: library of snips → three screens → combine the evidence → test with ASOs → find out how the two winners work.

lessons.title: The funnel: 831 → 80 → 9 → 5 → 2
lessons.goal: Understand how 831 lncRNAs were narrowed to 80 hits, nine candidates, five reproducible ones, and the final two (CHiLL1 and GCAWKR), and what each narrowing step asked.

lessons.title: Why it matters
lessons.goal: Say in your own words why lung cancer, long noncoding RNAs and ASO medicines make this a worthwhile study, and what it does and does not prove.

lessons.title: Cast of characters: the names you will see
lessons.goal: Meet the named lncRNAs and genes that keep reappearing (LINC00115, DNMBP-AS1, candidate numbers…) so no name is a surprise later.

lessons.title: Cells: the tiny rooms of life (nucleus vs cytoplasm)
lessons.goal: Know what a cell is, what the nucleus and cytoplasm are, and why "where in the cell" matters later in the paper.

lessons.title: How cells grow and divide: the cell cycle
lessons.goal: Describe the four phases G1, S, G2 and M, what a checkpoint is, and what "proliferation" means.

lessons.title: How cells die: apoptosis (and necrosis)
lessons.goal: Explain apoptosis as an orderly cell suicide, contrast it with necrosis, and name the early/late stages the paper counts.

lessons.title: DNA: the instruction book
lessons.goal: Describe DNA as a double-stranded chain of four letters, explain base pairing, and read "5′ end / 3′ end" and "bp".

lessons.title: Chromosomes, genes and the genome
lessons.goal: Explain chromosomes, genes, "locus" and the genome, and why a gene is a stretch of DNA you can point to.

lessons.title: Genome coordinates, genome versions (hg19/hg38) and strands
lessons.goal: Read an address like "Chr1: 765,000", know why genome versions (hg19, hg38) exist, and understand the two DNA strands, "same strand", "opposite strand" and "antisense".

lessons.title: From DNA to RNA: transcription, promoters and the TSS
lessons.goal: Explain transcription, RNA, the promoter and the transcription start site (TSS), and why "bidirectional promoters" matter.

lessons.title: Exons, introns, splicing and isoforms
lessons.goal: Describe how a transcript is cut and rejoined (splicing), what exons and introns are, and why one gene can have several isoforms.

lessons.title: Proteins, ORFs and protein-coding genes
lessons.goal: Explain how a protein-coding gene is read to make a protein, what an ORF is, and what "protein-coding potential" means.

lessons.title: Coding vs noncoding RNA
lessons.goal: Sort RNAs into "makes a protein" and "does something else", and meet the main noncoding kinds (ribosomal, microRNA, long noncoding).

lessons.title: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs): what they are and how they might work
lessons.goal: Define lncRNAs, explain the three big ideas for how they might act (guide, scaffold, decoy), cis vs trans, and meet the lung-cancer lncRNAs named in the Introduction.

lessons.title: Where RNAs live: nuclear vs cytoplasmic
lessons.goal: Explain why an RNA's position in the cell (nucleus or cytoplasm) is a clue to its job.

lessons.title: Gene catalogs: GENCODE, FANTOM CAT and BIGTranscriptome
lessons.goal: Explain what an annotation (a gene catalog) is, why different catalogs disagree on lncRNAs, and how the authors merged four of them.

lessons.title: Gene expression: genes turned up and down
lessons.goal: Explain "expression", "upregulated" and "downregulated", and the idea that every cell has the same DNA but uses different genes.

lessons.title: Switches on the DNA: enhancers, transcription factors and chromatin
lessons.goal: Explain enhancers, transcription factors and TFBS, chromatin, and the paper's phrase "DNA regulatory elements".

lessons.title: How to tell where a gene starts: CAGE, DNase I and ChromHMM
lessons.goal: Explain the three kinds of evidence the authors used to pick real lncRNA start sites: CAGE, DNase I hypersensitivity and ChromHMM marks.

lessons.title: What is cancer?
lessons.goal: Explain cancer as cells that keep dividing when they should not, what a tumor is, and why it is dangerous.

lessons.title: The hallmarks of cancer
lessons.goal: Describe the idea of "hallmarks" (abilities cancers acquire), meet the three the paper tests, and explain "phenotype" and "pleiotropic".

lessons.title: Oncogenes and tumor suppressors
lessons.goal: Use the gas-pedal and brake picture for oncogenes and tumor suppressors, and say what an "oncogenic lncRNA" is.

lessons.title: Mutations, copy-number gains (amplification) and losses (deletion)
lessons.goal: Explain point mutations, extra copies of DNA (amplification) and lost DNA (deletion), and what "recurrently amplified" means.

lessons.title: Lung cancer: NSCLC, adenocarcinoma, large cell carcinoma and metastasis
lessons.goal: Know the lung-cancer subtypes in the paper, what "metastasis", "invasion" and "migration" mean, and why NSCLC is a problem.

lessons.title: KRAS and EGFR mutations
lessons.goal: Explain what KRAS and EGFR do, what "KRAS+" means in the paper, and what targeted therapy is.

lessons.title: Chemotherapy, cisplatin, drug resistance and IC20 / IC30 / IC80
lessons.goal: Explain what cisplatin does, why cancers become resistant, and how IC20, IC30 and IC80 describe doses by their effect.

lessons.title: Cell lines vs normal lung cells (A549, H460, H441 and others)
lessons.goal: Explain what a cell line is, meet the lines used (A549, H460, H441, HEK293T) and the normal-cell controls (HBEC3-KT, MRC-5, CCD-16Lu), and the idea of "cell background".

lessons.title: Growing cells in 2D, 3D spheroids and organoids
lessons.goal: Contrast flat 2D cultures, 3D spheroids and organoids, and explain why 3D models are considered more faithful.

lessons.title: Patient-derived xenografts and immunodeficient mice
lessons.goal: Explain what a PDX is, why "immunodeficient" mice are needed, and how the BE874 organoids were made.

lessons.title: Patient data collections: TCGA, TANRIC, PCAWG, CCLE and GEO
lessons.goal: Explain what each public data collection contains and which question the paper asks of each one.

lessons.title: Tumor vs normal tissue, survival and tumor subtypes
lessons.goal: Explain "tumor versus adjacent normal", "survival analysis" and "tumor subtype", including the PI / PP / TRU labels.

lessons.title: CRISPR-Cas9 and guide RNAs
lessons.goal: Explain CRISPR-Cas9 as scissors steered by a guide RNA, and "loss of function".

lessons.title: CRISPR deletion with paired guides (DECKO): why delete the TSS?
lessons.goal: Explain CRISPR-del, paired guides (pgRNAs), DECKO, and the paper's reasons for deleting the TSS instead of the whole gene.

lessons.title: CRISPRi and Cas13 (only as far as the paper needs them)
lessons.goal: Say what CRISPRi and Cas13 are in one sentence each and why the paper mentions them.

lessons.title: Plasmids and lentivirus: delivering instructions into cells
lessons.goal: Explain plasmids and lentivirus as delivery trucks, and how HEK293T cells are used to make the virus (conceptually).

lessons.title: Transduction, MOI and antibiotic selection
lessons.goal: Explain transduction vs transfection, why a low MOI (0.3) means mostly one guide per cell, and how puromycin / blasticidin select cells.

lessons.title: Fluorescent proteins: GFP, mCherry and BFP
lessons.goal: Explain fluorescent proteins as glowing name-tags and how GFP, mCherry and BFP are used here.

lessons.title: Flow cytometry and FACS: counting and sorting cells one by one
lessons.goal: Explain how a flow cytometer reads each cell's light signal and how FACS sorts cells into tubes.

lessons.title: Pooled screens: testing thousands of suspects in one dish
lessons.goal: Explain the logic of a pooled CRISPR screen: a library, one perturbation per cell, a selection, and counting.

lessons.title: Libraries, guides per target and coverage
lessons.goal: Explain "depth" (10 guides per target), "coverage" (cells per guide), and how libDECKO-NSCLC1 was designed and cloned (conceptually).

lessons.title: From cells to counts: PCR, sequencing and read counts
lessons.goal: Follow a screen sample from cells to a table of guide counts: DNA, PCR, sequencing reads, time points.

lessons.title: Dropout vs positive selection screens
lessons.goal: Explain how a "dropout" screen and a "positive selection" screen are read, and what "depleted" and "enriched" mean for guides.

lessons.title: The proliferation screens: dropout and CFSE
lessons.goal: Explain how dropout and CFSE screens both measure growth, and what "fast-growing" and "slow-growing" cells look like under CFSE.

lessons.title: The cisplatin screens: survival and death
lessons.goal: Explain the two complementary cisplatin screens: "survival" at IC30 / IC80 and "death" at IC20.

lessons.title: The migration screen and the transwell assay
lessons.goal: Explain how a transwell (Boyden chamber) separates fast and slow migrators, and how that becomes a screen.

lessons.title: Controls in the screen: neutral, positive, and ORF vs TSS targeting
lessons.goal: Explain neutral and positive controls, why AAVS1 and RPS5 were used, and why controls were targeted two ways (ORF and promoter).

lessons.title: ASOs: how a short strand can switch a gene off
lessons.goal: Explain how an ASO pairs with an RNA and gets it destroyed, what LNA chemistry adds, and what "knockdown" means.

lessons.title: Using ASOs well: two ASOs per target, controls, knockdown % and cocktails
lessons.goal: Explain why each lncRNA needs two ASOs, the non-targeting control, "knockdown %", on-target vs off-target, and ASO cocktails.

lessons.title: DNA gels and genotyping PCR: did the deletion happen?
lessons.goal: Read a DNA gel: bands, ladder, wild-type vs deleted bands, and what the genotyping PCR in Figure 1E shows.

lessons.title: qRT-PCR: measuring how much RNA is left
lessons.goal: Explain reverse transcription, qPCR, normalisation to a housekeeping gene, and "relative expression".

lessons.title: The competition assay
lessons.goal: Explain how mixing green and red cells 1:1 and tracking the ratio over days measures fitness.

lessons.title: Luminescence viability assays (CellTiter-Glo)
lessons.goal: Explain how an ATP-based glow reading estimates living cells and how "relative growth" is built from it.

lessons.title: Annexin V: catching cells in the act of dying
lessons.goal: Explain how Annexin V plus a viability dye separate alive, early-apoptotic, late-apoptotic and necrotic cells by flow cytometry.

lessons.title: Cell-cycle staining: DAPI and Ki-67
lessons.goal: Explain how DNA content (DAPI) and Ki-67 sort cells into G1, S and G2/M.

lessons.title: Crystal violet migration assay
lessons.goal: Explain the low-throughput migration assay: stain the cells that crossed, dissolve the dye, read absorbance.

lessons.title: RNA-FISH and microscopy
lessons.goal: Explain how fluorescent probes make single RNA molecules visible in a cell and how a cytoplasmic/nuclear ratio is derived.

lessons.title: Cell fractionation: nuclear vs cytoplasmic RNA
lessons.goal: Explain how cells are split into nucleus and cytoplasm and how MALAT1 and GAPDH serve as markers.

lessons.title: Overexpression and rescue experiments
lessons.goal: Explain what a rescue experiment tests, why it can fail even when the biology is real, and the paper's possible explanations.

lessons.title: RNA-seq and differentially expressed genes (DEGs)
lessons.goal: Explain RNA-seq as counting every RNA at once, what a DEG is, and what the two ASOs agreeing means.

lessons.title: Pathway enrichment: KEGG, MSigDB and transcription-factor sites
lessons.goal: Explain how a list of changed genes is tested against "pathway" lists (KEGG, MSigDB, TFBS) and how to read the result.

lessons.title: What the named pathways roughly do (p53, MAPK, PI3K–Akt, mTORC1 …)
lessons.goal: Give a one-line job description for every pathway the paper names (p53, MAPK, PI3K–Akt, VEGF, mTORC1, glycolysis, EMT, G2-M checkpoint …).

lessons.title: Counting RNA fairly: CPM, TPM and FPKM
lessons.goal: Explain why raw counts must be normalised and what CPM, TPM and FPKM each correct for.

lessons.title: Fold change and log2
lessons.goal: Compute and interpret fold change and log2 fold change, and see why log2 makes up and down changes symmetrical.

lessons.title: Replicates, mean, SD and error bars
lessons.goal: Distinguish biological from technical replicates, read mean ± SD error bars, understand n, medians and percentiles.

lessons.title: Correlation and regression lines
lessons.goal: Read Pearson R, the trendline, and what "R = 0.66" says (and does not say).

lessons.title: Z-scores
lessons.goal: Explain a Z-score as "how many SDs from typical" and how the paper scales screen results against neutral controls.

lessons.title: p-values, "significant", "ns" and scientific notation
lessons.goal: Say what a p-value is (and is not), what "ns" and asterisks mean, and read numbers like 2.2e-16.

lessons.title: One- vs two-tailed tests and t-tests (including Welch's)
lessons.goal: Explain one-tailed vs two-tailed, what a t-test compares, and when Welch's version is used.

lessons.title: Rank-based tests: Wilcoxon, Mann–Whitney and Kruskal–Wallis
lessons.goal: Explain why rank-based (non-parametric) tests are used and what Wilcoxon, Mann–Whitney and Kruskal–Wallis compare.

lessons.title: Overlap and enrichment tests: Fisher's exact and hypergeometric
lessons.goal: Explain the "overlap by chance" question and how Fisher's exact and the hypergeometric test answer it.

lessons.title: Many tests at once: multiple testing and FDR (why FDR < 0.2)
lessons.goal: Explain the multiple-testing problem, the false discovery rate, Benjamini–Hochberg, q-values, and the reasoning for a lenient FDR < 0.2 cutoff.

lessons.title: ROC curves and AUC
lessons.goal: Read a ROC curve and AUC: true-positive rate, false-positive rate, and what AUC 0.82 vs 0.54 mean.

lessons.title: Combining screens: rank aggregation, Brown's method and the harmonic-mean p-value (TPP)
lessons.goal: Explain, with minimal math, how TPP combines effect size and significance across screens into one FDR-controlled ranking.

lessons.title: Practice: decoding the statistics in the figure legends
lessons.goal: Apply everything: decode five real legends (what test, what n, what the error bars are, what the stars mean).

lessons.title: Bar charts with error bars
lessons.goal: Read bars, error bars, labels and the control bar; practised on Figures 1F, 3F and 5E.

lessons.title: Box plots and violin plots
lessons.goal: Read median, box, whiskers and the violin outline; practised on Figures 2F and 4F.

lessons.title: Scatter plots with a regression line
lessons.goal: Read axes, points, the trendline and R; practised on Figures 2E, 2H and 6E.

lessons.title: Contour (density) plots
lessons.goal: Read contour lines as "crowding" of points; practised on Figure 4E.

lessons.title: Volcano-style plots
lessons.goal: Read the two axes (fold change on x, significance on y) and the cutoff line; practised on Figure 2G.

lessons.title: Heatmaps
lessons.goal: Read color scales, rows and columns, and patterns; practised on Figures 5A and 5H.

lessons.title: Time courses and line plots
lessons.goal: Read growth curves, error bars and p-labels over time; practised on Figures 3B, 3D, 5C and 5G.

lessons.title: ROC curves in a figure
lessons.goal: Read the curve, the diagonal and the AUC table; practised on Figure 4B.

lessons.title: Ternary and petal plots
lessons.goal: Read a triangle plot (three hallmarks at three corners) and a petal plot; practised on Figure 4C.

lessons.title: UpSet plots
lessons.goal: Read a UpSet plot (overlaps of many sets); practised on Figure 2I.

lessons.title: Stacked bars and composition charts
lessons.goal: Read stacked percentage bars and counts; practised on Figures 1C, 4D, 4H and 6G.

lessons.title: Genome-browser tracks
lessons.goal: Read a gene-locus picture: scale, strands, exons, TSS arrow, primers, ASOs and guides; practised on Figures 1E, 3A, 5D and 6A.

lessons.title: DNA gels in a figure
lessons.goal: Read the ladder, the wild-type and deletion bands in Figure 1E.

lessons.title: Flow cytometry plots
lessons.goal: Read a dot plot with a sorting gate; practised on Figure 1D.

lessons.title: Microscopy and FISH images
lessons.goal: Read scale bars, arrows and labels in cell images; practised on Figures 6B, 3E, 5E and 6L.

lessons.title: The small print: n, error bars, P labels, asterisks and "ns"
lessons.goal: Read the details that decide how much a figure proves.

lessons.title: The paper's logic as a chain: claim → evidence → figure panel
lessons.goal: Lay out the paper's main claims, the evidence for each, and the exact panel that supports it.

lessons.title: Every control and why it exists
lessons.goal: List every control in the paper (neutral, positive, non-targeting, normal cells, markers, vectors) and say what mistake each one rules out.

lessons.title: DNA vs RNA effects: why ASOs were needed
lessons.goal: Explain how the authors separated a DNA effect from an RNA effect and the LINC00115 vs RP11-206L10.11 example.

lessons.title: ASO off-target effects and how the paper handles them
lessons.goal: Explain the on-target evidence (two ASOs, several cell lines, correlated RNA-seq) and what is not tested (rescue failed).

lessons.title: Cell-line-specific effects and background independence
lessons.goal: Explain why the authors screened two lines, integrated across hallmarks, and added more lines and 3D models.

lessons.title: The limitations section, line by line
lessons.goal: List the limitations the authors state and add the ones a skeptical reader would add.

lessons.title: The declared patent and conflict of interest
lessons.goal: Read the declaration of interests, explain what a patent application and a conflict of interest are, and how to treat them fairly.

lessons.title: Experiments that would strengthen the work
lessons.goal: Propose concrete follow-up experiments and say which weakness each would fix.

lessons.title: Strengths vs weaknesses: essay-ready summary
lessons.goal: Write and judge a balanced strengths-versus-weaknesses essay using evidence from the paper.

terms.term: in vitro / in vivo / ex vivo
aliases: in vitro / in vivo / ex vivo
